repo.description: The most widely used Python to C compiler
repo.name: cython

body:
This bundles 2 things into 1 (I can split it if needed) but my justification is "implementation" and "example use".

1. Add `implicit_param` option to template parameters
    
    This is to avoid Cython generating C++ code like
    
    ```
    f<int>(...)
    ```
    
    which is sometimes the wrong thing to do. For reasons probably
    lost to history, it only applies to free functions and not methods.
    I did consider adding `explicit_param` to let you go the other
    way on methods but I don't think there's immediate demand.

2. C11 standard atomics

    These are implemented in C as type-generic macros so behave
    quite a bit like templates but can't use our template code-paths.
    I think the `implicit_param` options works reasonably well for these.

    Finishes #7630

comment_data.body:
This (and most of the other similar functions with return types) isn't quite perfect in that it'll be inferred as `atomic_int` rather than `int`. I don't really think there's a good way around that and I think it's close enough to right that it'll practically work.

But if the type is inferred rather than user-specified it may unnecessarily become atomic which will be slightly inefficient.

+    ctypedef unsigned char atomic_uint_fast8_t

+    ctypedef unsigned short atomic_uint_fast16_t
+    ctypedef int atomic_int_fast32_t 
+    ctypedef unsigned int atomic_uint_fast32_t 
+    ctypedef long long atomic_int_fast64_t 
+    ctypedef unsigned long long atomic_uint_fast64_t

+cdef extern from "<stdatomic.h>" nogil:

+

+    bint atomic_is_lock_free[cython.implicit_param[T]](volatile const T* obj)
+    void atomic_store[cython.implicit_param[T], cython.implicit_param[U]](
+        volatile T* obj, U desired)

+        volatile T* obj, U desired, memory_order order)

comment_data.body:
One solution to that would be to think about a `cython.no_infer` return type (name to be decided) that says something like "this function returns something that isn't known to Cython, but trust me - the assignments I've made work". It's difficult to see how that would work for anything that requires temps though.

I think the slightly inaccurate types here are fine, but there might be other ways to express this kind of idea.
